messages:
devon: Heads-up — we're seeing a cluster-wide retry spike for the inference fleet in us-west-2 around 10:05 UTC. App metrics show /v1/infer 5xx rate jumped x10 and client-side retries spiked. No deploys at the time.

maria: Seeing the same. TL;DR: a small subset of GPU nodes are getting hammered while others sit idle. Latency to endpoints uneven, lots of client TCP retransmits in netstat.

sam: Any network errors on the nodes? packets dropped / MTU mismatches?

leo: Initial digs: kernel shows ECN marked packets increasing on the fastpath. `tc -s qdisc` shows drops and ECN marks on `ipvs` facing veths. Paste: ```
qdisc pfifo_fast 0: dev eth0 root refcnt 2 bands 3 priomap  1 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2
 Sent 123456789 bytes  packets 987654
 backlog 0b 0p requeues 0
 backlog 0b 0p requeues 0
  backlog 0b 0p requeues 0
  DSCP 0x00 0x... ECN marked: 3421
```

devon: Interesting — ECN spikes could explain middleboxes or NIC offload reacting and forcing retransmits which confuse IPVS connection tracking. Did k8s-proxy notice conn-state churn?

k8s-bot: ipvsadm -l --stats snapshot at 10:04: ```
TCP 6379 rr
  10.0.4.22:5000 -> [10.0.8.11:5000] conns 1200 packets 1.2M
  10.0.4.22:5000 -> [10.0.8.12:5000] conns 45 packets 32k
  10.0.4.22:5000 -> [10.0.8.13:5000] conns 90 packets 64k
```

maria: That matches the app failures: 10.0.8.11 (one GPU node) is taking ~95% of flows. Others showing frequent conn resets.

sam: GPU node 10.0.8.11 — check driver + RDMA state. If RDMA NIC is toggling ECN/thresholds, it might push kernel to prefer one path. Also check `ethtool -k` for GRO/GSO/TSO differences.

leo: Ran `ethtool -k 10.0.8.11` — TSO/GSO enabled, but `rx-checksumming` dropped intermittently. Logs show NIC firmware reclaimed queues at 10:03:54.

devon: Could that cause packets to be ECN-marked and then TCP fallback produces retransmits which IPVS treats as new connections, skewing the hash?

maria: Also observed iptables conntrack entries flapping for the service. conntrack count for that svc jumped 8x, then freed.

sam: Quick mitigation: temporarily disable ECN on affected nodes to see if distribution normalizes. `sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_ecn=0` on a small canary subset.

leo: Doing canary on 10.0.8.11/12/13 now. Will report within 2 mins.

ops-bot: deploy-checklist: rolling sysctl change to canary group initiated by leo at 10:12 UTC.

leo: Canary done: 10.0.8.11 set tcp_ecn=0. Early signs: ipvs stats leveling out, packets to 8.11 dropping overall but balancing across 8.12/8.13. App 5xx rate trending down.

devon: Good. If ECN off fixes distribution, we should look at NIC firmware/drivers and RDMA interaction. We need a postmortem: root cause likely NIC queue reclamation + ECN causing IPVS connection churn.

maria: Agreed. Follow-ups: 1) schedule firmware roll for affected NIC model, 2) audit ipvs conntrack churn metrics for last 30d, 3) add ECN alerting tied to sudden increase in ipvs per-backend skew.

sam: Also add a temporary RBAC runbook entry: how to toggle tcp_ecn and validate ipvs `ipvsadm -l --stats`.

leo: Will open a tracking ticket and attach the logs/`ethtool`/`dmesg` snippets. Ticket includes steps to repro in staging with RDMA-enabled workloads.

devon: Thanks everyone. Leaving ECN disabled on the canary nodes until firmware is confirmed. If anyone sees a related client-side retry bubble, ping @oncall. :thumbsup:
